summary: Rebecca Sundén works in Indology and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Hamburg, where she is attested in 2026 as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin.

Reginald A. Ray is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied under teachers including Eliade, Kitagawa, and Chögyam Trungpa, and taught at the University of Colorado Boulder (attested 2001–2002) and Naropa University (attested 2001–2006).
Reginald Edward Enthoven (1869–1952) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Wellington College from around 1883 to 1887 and at New College in 1887.

Reginald Heber (1783–1826) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He earned an M.A. from Brasenose College and a D.D. from the University of Oxford (~1800–1823), and served as a Fellow at All Souls College, Oxford, in 1805.

Reginald Stephen Copleston (1845–1925) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Merton College and Exeter College, Oxford, he was a Fellow at St John's College, Oxford (1870–1875) and President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (~1885–1902).
Rei Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University (~1949–1953), where he later served as a professor from around 1974 to 2000.
Reiho Masunaga (1902–1981) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied under Kaiten Nukariya (~1922–1930) and taught at Komazawa University from around 1934 to 1972.

Reiko Ohnuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at UC Berkeley, with Padmanabh S. Jaini, and earned her Ph.D. under Luis Oscar Gómez at the University of Michigan, later holding posts at UT Austin, Alabama, and Dartmouth.

Reimon Yuki (1902–1992) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Daijō Tokiwa at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the Academy of Oriental Culture, Kyoto Women's University, and the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.

Reiner Wiehl (1929–2010) was a philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Nancy and Goethe University Frankfurt, later serving as Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1969–1977) and Heidelberg University (appointed 1977).

Reinhold F. G. Müller (1882–1966) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. After studying at Berlin, Innsbruck, and Greifswald, he was an assistant at the University of Greifswald (~1909–1911) and a Privatdozent in medicine at Leipzig (1942).
Reinhold Grünendahl is an Indology scholar who held positions at the Free University of Berlin (attested 1983–1984) and the Göttingen State and University Library (attested 2008).

Reinhold Klotz (1807–1870) was a linguistics, history, and archaeology scholar. He completed his Habilitation at the University of Leipzig, where he became an assistant professor in 1832 and an außerordentlicher Professor from 1849 to 1870.

Reinhold Niebuhr (1892–1971) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Elmhurst University, Eden Theological Seminary, and Yale Divinity School, and served on the faculty at Union Theological Seminary from around 1928 to 1960.

Reinhold Rost (1822–1896) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Jena. He served as Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society, Professor of Sanskrit at King's College London, and Librarian of the India Office (1869–1893).

Reinhold Trautmann (1883–1951) was a linguist who studied at Königsberg, Freiburg, Berlin, and Göttingen. He held professorships at Prague, Königsberg, and Leipzig, followed by a chair at Jena and leading the GDR Academy of Sciences.

Reinhold von Stackelberg (1860–1907) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist. He studied at Tartu, Leipzig, and Strasbourg, later serving as Privatdozent at Leipzig (1891–1892) and Professor of Persian at the Lazarev Institute (1894).
Reirin Yamada (1889–1979) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He later served as president of Komazawa Junior College from around 1950 to 1968.
Remeen Firoz is an Indology scholar attested in 2026 as a Ph.D. student at the Australian National University, studying under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron.
Rena Aronovna Aulova (1927–1997) was an Indologist and linguist. She studied at the National University of Uzbekistan from around 1944 to 1949 and served there as a Docent in 1979.
